function binary_search(arr, target)
    local low = 1
    local high = #arr
    while low <= high do
        local mid = math.floor((low + high) / 2)
        if arr[mid] == target then
            return mid - 1
        elseif arr[mid] < target then
            low = mid + 1
        else
            high = mid - 1
        end
    end
    return -1
end

function bubble_sort(arr)
    local n = #arr
    for i = 1, n do
        local swapped = false
        for j = 1, n - i do
            if arr[j] > arr[j + 1] then
                arr[j], arr[j + 1] = arr[j + 1], arr[j]
                swapped = true
            end
        end
        if not swapped then break end
    end
    return arr
end

function merge(left, right)
    local result = {}
    local i, j = 1, 1
    while i <= #left and j <= #right do
        if left[i] <= right[j] then
            result[#result + 1] = left[i]
            i = i + 1
        else
            result[#result + 1] = right[j]
            j = j + 1
        end
    end
    while i <= #left do result[#result + 1] = left[i]; i = i + 1 end
    while j <= #right do result[#result + 1] = right[j]; j = j + 1 end
    return result
end

    if #arr <= 1 then return arr end

    for k = 1, mid do left[#left + 1] = arr[k] end
    for k = mid + 1, #arr do right[#right + 1] = arr[k] end
    left = merge_sort(left)
    right = merge_sort(right)
    return merge(left, right)
end

    local pivot = arr[high]
    local i = low - 1
    for j = low, high - 1 do
        if arr[j] <= pivot then
            i = i + 1
            arr[i], arr[j] = arr[j], arr[i]
        end
    end

    return i + 1

sieve_of_eratosthenes._description: Implement the Sieve of Eratosthenes to find all prime numbers up to a given limit N. Mark multiples of each prime starting from its square, then collect all unmarked numbers.
sieve_of_eratosthenes.Lua:
function sieve(n)
    local is_prime = {}
    for i = 0, n do is_prime[i] = true end
    is_prime[0] = false
    is_prime[1] = false
    local p = 2
    while p * p <= n do
        if is_prime[p] then
            for i = p * p, n, p do
                is_prime[i] = false
            end
        end
        p = p + 1
    end
    local primes = {}
    for i = 2, n do
        if is_prime[i] then primes[#primes + 1] = i end
    end
    return primes
end

function matrix_multiply(a, b)
    local rows_a = #a
    local cols_a = #a[1]
    local cols_b = #b[1]
    local result = {}
    for i = 1, rows_a do
        result[i] = {}
        for j = 1, cols_b do
            result[i][j] = 0
            for k = 1, cols_a do
                result[i][j] = result[i][j] + a[i][k] * b[k][j]
            end
        end
    end
    return result
end

edit_distance._description: Compute the Levenshtein edit distance between two strings using dynamic programming. Find the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions, and substitutions needed.
edit_distance.Lua:
function edit_distance(s1, s2)
    local m = #s1
    local n = #s2
    local dp = {}
    for i = 0, m do
        dp[i] = {}
        for j = 0, n do dp[i][j] = 0 end
        dp[i][0] = i
    end
    for j = 0, n do dp[0][j] = j end
    for i = 1, m do
        for j = 1, n do
            if s1:sub(i, i) == s2:sub(j, j) then
                dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1]
            else
                dp[i][j] = 1 + math.min(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1], dp[i - 1][j - 1])
            end
        end
    end
    return dp[m][n]
end

function topological_sort(graph, n)
    local in_degree = {}

    for u = 1, n do

            in_degree[v] = in_degree[v] + 1

    local front = 1
    for v = 1, n do

        order[#order + 1] = u
        for _, v in ipairs(graph[u]) do
            in_degree[v] = in_degree[v] - 1
            if in_degree[v] == 0 then

        end
    end
    return order
end

def nqueens(n):
    cols = [False] * n
    diag1 = [False] * (2 * n - 1)
    diag2 = [False] * (2 * n - 1)
    count = 0

    def backtrack(row):
        nonlocal count
        if row == n:
            count += 1
            return
        for col in range(n):
            if cols[col] or diag1[row - col + n - 1] or diag2[row + col]:
                continue
            cols[col] = diag1[row - col + n - 1] = diag2[row + col] = True
            backtrack(row + 1)
            cols[col] = diag1[row - col + n - 1] = diag2[row + col] = False

    backtrack(0)
    return count

function build_lps(pattern)
    local n = #pattern
    local lps = {}
    for i = 1, n do lps[i] = 0 end
    local len = 0
    local i = 2
    while i <= n do
        if pattern:sub(i, i) == pattern:sub(len + 1, len + 1) then
            len = len + 1
            lps[i] = len
            i = i + 1
        else

            else
                lps[i] = 0
                i = i + 1
            end
        end

    local lps = build_lps(pattern)

    local i = 1

    while i <= #text do

            j = j + 1

        if j > #pattern then
            results[#results + 1] = i - #pattern - 1

        elseif i <= #text and text:sub(i, i) ~= pattern:sub(j, j) then

function longest_increasing_subsequence(arr)
    local n = #arr
    if n == 0 then return 0 end
    local dp = {}
    for i = 1, n do dp[i] = 1 end
    for i = 2, n do
        for j = 1, i - 1 do
            if arr[j] < arr[i] and dp[j] + 1 > dp[i] then
                dp[i] = dp[j] + 1
            end
        end
    end

    for i = 2, n do

    end
    return result
end
